title: Template Context and Performance knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Template Context and Performance”?
options: Template Context and Performance should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Template Context and Performance helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Template Context and Performance means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Template Context and Performance removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Template Context and Performance helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Template Context and Performance is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Avoiding repeated expensive expressions” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Avoiding repeated expensive expressions” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Avoiding repeated expensive expressions” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Avoiding repeated expensive expressions” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Avoiding repeated expensive expressions” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Avoiding repeated expensive expressions” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Avoiding repeated expensive expressions” under Template Context and Performance. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Template Context and Performance”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
